content: Take dicloxacillin with a large glass of water (at least 4 ounces or 120 milliliters) at least one hour before or two hours after a meal. Ensure that you remain sitting or standing upright while taking dicloxacillin. Do not take this medication while lying down or immediately before going to bed. Only take dicloxacillin if it has been prescribed to you by a healthcare provider, and follow the prescribed instructions carefully. Do not share dicloxacillin with others, even if they have the same condition, as it may harm them. Keep this medication out of the reach of children. Before using dicloxacillin, inform your healthcare provider about all your health conditions and any prescription or over-the-counter (OTC) medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, or other supplements you are taking. This information will help your provider determine if dicloxacillin is appropriate for you. Dicloxacillin may interact with other medications and supplements. Always discuss with your healthcare provider if you are using any of the following: tetracyclines (e.g., tetracycline, doxycycline, minocycline, omadacycline, sarecycline), probenecid (commonly used for gout), or warfarin (a blood thinner). This may not be a complete list of potential interactions, so consult your provider for more details. If you are allergic to penicillin or other medications, have asthma, experience nausea, vomiting, or gastrointestinal issues, have a history of antibiotic-associated diarrhea, or have kidney problems, inform your healthcare provider. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, let your provider know, as it is unclear how dicloxacillin may affect pregnancy or an unborn baby. Your provider will advise you on whether you should take dicloxacillin during pregnancy. If you are breastfeeding or planning to breastfeed, inform your provider, as dicloxacillin passes into breast milk. Dicloxacillin is best absorbed on an empty stomach. Take it with a large glass of water at least one hour before or two hours after meals. It is unknown if alcohol consumption affects dicloxacillin, but heavy drinking can weaken your immune response and make it harder for your body to fight infections. If you accidentally take too much dicloxacillin, seek medical help immediately, call 911, or contact a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take only the next scheduled dose. Do not take double or extra doses. It is crucial to complete the full prescribed course of dicloxacillin, even if your symptoms improve or resolve, to reduce the risk of future infections becoming resistant to dicloxacillin or similar medications.
